newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom taking loan for S.African deal.
newsitem.headline: Telekom taking loan for S.African deal.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd will take a short-term loan of $400 million to partly finance its acquisition of a 12 percent stake in South Africa's utility Telkom, Telekom's chief executive said on Thursday.

"We are taking a short-term bridging loan for the $400 million but will also be considering a long-term loan. It depends on the market," Telekom chief executive Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali was quoted in Cape Town by the national Bernama news agency as saying.
The cost for the 12 percent stake is around $504. The remainder of the financing would come from internal funds, according to Mohamed Said.
Telekom jointly bought a 30 percent stake in Telkom with U.S.-based SBC Communications Inc for $1.26 billion.
Mohamed Said said Telekom would continue to move into new areas as there are many opportunities in Asia and Africa.

"Telekom Malaysia is also eyeing the upcoming privatisation programme in Kenya, which is sometime in August, and in Zimbabwe next year," he told Malaysian reporters before the signing ceremony for the Telkom acquisition.
Telekom's other overseas ventures are in Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Malawi, Ghana, Guinea, India and Cambodia.
